items.text: Goods made abroad should be able to compete on equal terms with goods made at home.
items.rationale: Core free-trade view of classical liberals, libertarians, many social democrats and cosmopolitan socialists; applies to any country, ideal or actual.

items.text: Trade across borders should be completely free, with no tariffs or import limits of any kind.
items.note: Tariff: a tax charged on goods brought in from another country.
items.rationale: Strong unilateral free trade (Cobdenite liberals, anarcho-capitalists, some anarchists who reject borders); mirrors glo-09; mild free-traders may split by frame.

items.text: Foreign investors should be able to own businesses on the same terms as local investors.
items.rationale: National-treatment principle endorsed by market liberals and open-economy developmentalists; frames may differ where people distrust specific foreign investors today.

items.text: Money should move freely between countries, with no limits on where people invest it.
items.rationale: Full capital mobility (libertarians, financial liberals); mirrors glo-11 capital controls; works for any economy.

items.text: If imports make everyday goods cheaper for most families, that gain should count for more than the local jobs lost.
items.rationale: Pro-Open condition (consumer gains); free-traders accept this trade-off as a fair statement; here-and-now answers may track local job markets.

items.text: If a foreign buyer offers the best price for a large local company, the sale should go ahead.
items.rationale: Open-capital view (market liberals, shareholder-rights advocates); condition favours Open (best offer); plausible frame split given real-world strategic worries.

items.text: If a local industry can survive only behind tariffs, it should be left to shrink or close.
items.note: Tariff: a tax charged on goods brought in from another country.
items.rationale: Pro-Open condition (sheltered inefficiency); strong because it accepts closures; endorsed by free-traders and creative-destruction liberals in both frames.

items.text: Goods made at home should have an advantage over imported goods, for example through tariffs or buy-local rules.
items.note: Tariff: a tax charged on goods brought in from another country.
items.rationale: Mainstream protectionism (economic nationalists, labour-left, distributists, eco-localists); 'buy-local rules' keeps it answerable for non-state communities; mirrors glo-01.

items.text: A country should produce nearly everything it needs at home, even when imports would be cheaper.
items.rationale: Strong self-sufficiency (autarkists, some national-conservatives, Juche/self-reliance and degrowth localists); mirrors glo-02; feasibility may split frames.

items.text: Major companies should be owned mainly by people who live in the country.
items.rationale: Local-ownership view (economic nationalists, communitarians, some socialists and populists); mirrors glo-03; agent-neutral arrangement wording.

items.text: Money moving in and out of a country should be tightly controlled to protect the local economy.
items.rationale: Strong capital controls (developmental-state advocates, post-Keynesians, some nationalists); mirrors glo-04; works under both frames.

items.text: If cheap imports are wiping out a local industry, that industry should be protected from them.
items.rationale: Pro-Protected condition (industry collapse); fair statement for protectionists and labour-left; mirrors glo-05; frame split likely for moderate free-traders.

items.text: If money from abroad is pushing up local housing prices, foreign buying should be limited.
items.rationale: Pro-Protected condition (housing affordability); endorsed across left populists and national-conservatives; often answered differently here-and-now.

items.text: If a crisis could cut off supplies from abroad, key goods like medicine and food should be made at home, even at much higher cost.
items.rationale: Pro-Protected condition (supply-chain security); strong via 'much higher cost'; endorsed by resilience hawks, nationalists and localists; ideal frame stipulates hard situations so it reads in both.
